findings.requirement: Preserve valid transfers and existing trigger semantics while validating transaction effects.
findings.evidence: The tokenizer discards U+00A0 as whitespace, although SQLite accepts it as an unquoted identifier. Reproduction: initialize accounts ('one','a',100) and ('one','b',0); execute Python SQL expression "CREATE TRIGGER " + chr(160) + " DELETE ON transfers BEGIN SELECT RAISE(FAIL,'delete gate'); END" and SQL "CREATE TRIGGER mirror AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN INSERT OR REPLACE INTO transfers SELECT * FROM transfers; END"; call vault.transfer(path,'one','a','b',10,'k'). Both .baseline and .pre-repair succeed with balances 90/10 and one receipt/audit row. The candidate raises IntegrityError('delete gate'); its CLI exits 2. Replacing only the Unicode trigger name with 'gate' makes the candidate succeed. Losing the name causes event extraction to read ON instead of DELETE, so the guard incorrectly fires this trigger for an implicit REPLACE deletion. Failed calls roll back completely.
findings.suggested_fix: Match SQLite's whitespace and identifier tokenization, preserve non-ASCII identifier characters, and verify event extraction. Add a regression using the demonstrated identifier and logically unchanged REPLACE operation. Distinguish the newly demonstrated controls: this SQLite accepts vertical tab (U+000B) and U+FEFF as token separators, but treats U+00A0 as an identifier character. Your pre-repair version passes both separator controls; retain them. Also retain dollar names and the public total_changes() control. Fix only the tokenizer/event-boundary delta.
